top_news.dek: Anthropic is making 'auto mode' the default setting for Claude Code sessions across Pro, Max, and Team plans starting August 14th.
top_news.brief: The shift signals increased confidence in the agent's ability to autonomously execute coding tasks. Users are encouraged to review safety configurations as the tool moves toward more hands-off operation.

top_news.title: Google's DiffusionGemma proves you don't need to train from scratch to build a text diffusion model
top_news.dek: Google DeepMind retrofitted the Gemma 4 model into a diffusion-based architecture using less than 10% of the original training budget.
top_news.brief: DiffusionGemma generates 256 tokens in parallel, achieving speeds of approximately 1,500 tokens per second. While it demonstrates the viability of repurposing existing autoregressive weights for diffusion, the model currently underperforms compared to the original Gemma 4 on reasoning-heavy benchmarks.
top_news.image_alt: Scatter plot comparing token generation speed versus accuracy for DiffusionGemma.

top_news.title: Meet Shepherd: An Open-Source Python Substrate That Lets Meta-Agents Fork, Replay, and Revert Any Agent Run
top_news.dek: Shepherd is an open-source Python runtime that enables stateful branching, replaying, and reverting for autonomous agent workflows.
top_news.brief: Developed by researchers at Northeastern and Stanford, Shepherd addresses the difficulty of managing agent state during long-running tasks. By capturing the full execution environment, it allows developers to fork or revert agent runs to specific steps, avoiding the cost of full restarts or inefficient forward-patching.
top_news.image_alt: Diagram illustrating agent state branching and replay functionality in Shepherd.

members.summary: Backflip AI has released an AI model that converts 3D scans into fully editable, parametric CAD models, a process that normally takes significant time and expertise. According to CEO Greg Mark, most factories have digital models for less than one percent of their parts. The startup, backed by $30 million in funding, offers its tool as an add-in for Autodesk Fusion. primary.title: Fields Medalist who published a paper on AI-driven human extinction now works for OpenAI
primary.summary: Newly awarded Fields Medalist Jacob Tsimerman is leaving the University of Toronto to join OpenAI and work on AI safety. In a recent paper, he analyzes scenarios where AI could contribute to human extinction and calls for far more investment in safety research.
